metadata.title: Broken Replica Symmetry Bounds in the Mean Field Spin Glass Model (Guerra, 2002)
metadata.framework: Interpolation method proving that the Parisi replica symmetry breaking ansatz provides a lower bound on the free energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on arXiv:cond-mat/0205123 PDF text.

nodes.name: Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) model
nodes.statement: A mean-field spin glass with $N$ Ising spins $\sigma_i \in \{-1, +1\}$ and Hamiltonian $H_N(\sigma) = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} \sum_{1 \leq i < j \leq N} J_{ij} \sigma_i \sigma_j - h \sum_i \sigma_i$, where $J_{ij}$ are i.i.d. standard Gaussian random variables and $h$ is the external field. The quenched free energy per site is $-\beta f_N(\beta) = \frac{1}{N} \mathbb{E} \log Z_N(\beta)$.

nodes.name: Parisi replica symmetry breaking (RSB) ansatz
nodes.statement: The Parisi ansatz parameterizes the free energy by a non-decreasing function $x: [0,1] \to [0,1]$ (the functional order parameter). For $K$-step RSB, this is a step function with $K$ jumps at positions $0 = m_0 < m_1 < \cdots < m_K < m_{K+1} = 1$ with values $0 = q_0 < q_1 < \cdots < q_K < q_{K+1} = 1$. The Parisi functional $\mathcal{P}(\beta, x)$ gives the predicted free energy.

nodes.name: Guerra interpolation method
nodes.statement: Introduce an interpolation parameter $t \in [0,1]$ and a family of Hamiltonians $H_N(t, \sigma)$ that smoothly connects the SK model at $t=1$ to a solvable reference system at $t=0$. The reference system involves independent Gaussian fields matching the Parisi RSB structure at each level.

nodes.name: Parisi formula as a lower bound (Guerra bound)
nodes.statement: For any $K$-step Parisi order parameter and any $N$: $\frac{1}{N} \mathbb{E} \log Z_N(\beta) \geq \mathcal{P}_K(\beta)$, where $\mathcal{P}_K$ is the Parisi functional evaluated at the $K$-step RSB ansatz. Taking $K \to \infty$ and optimizing over the functional order parameter: $\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N} \mathbb{E} \log Z_N(\beta) \geq \inf_x \mathcal{P}(\beta, x)$.

nodes.name: Proof of lower bound via interpolation
nodes.statement: Define an interpolating pressure $\phi_N(t)$ between the SK model and the Parisi reference system. Show that $\frac{d}{dt} \phi_N(t) \geq 0$ using convexity of the pressure in the Gaussian disorder and the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities (or a direct positivity argument on the derivative). Since $\phi_N(1)$ is the SK free energy and $\phi_N(0)$ is the Parisi expression, the bound follows.

nodes.name: Sum rule for the difference
nodes.statement: The difference between the true free energy and the Parisi expression is expressed as a sum rule: $\frac{1}{N} \mathbb{E} \log Z_N - \mathcal{P}_K = \int_0^1 R_N(t) \, dt$ where $R_N(t) \geq 0$ involves expectations of overlap-dependent quantities under the interpolating Gibbs measure.

nodes.name: Complementary to Talagrand's matching upper bound
nodes.statement: Guerra's lower bound, combined with Talagrand's matching upper bound (2006, Annals of Mathematics), proves the Parisi formula: $\lim_{N \to \infty} f_N(\beta) = \inf_x \mathcal{P}(\beta, x)$. Guerra provides the easier half; Talagrand's upper bound is significantly more technically demanding.

nodes.name: Ground state energy bound
nodes.statement: As a corollary, the interpolation method gives a variational bound on the ground state energy per site: $\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N} \mathbb{E} \min_\sigma H_N(\sigma) \leq -\beta \inf_x \mathcal{P}(\beta, x)$ in the $\beta \to \infty$ limit.

nodes.name: Simplicity of the interpolation argument
nodes.statement: The interpolation technique is remarkably simple compared to the replica method from physics. It avoids the non-rigorous replica trick entirely, instead using a direct probabilistic interpolation that yields rigorous bounds. The same technique was previously used by Guerra to prove the thermodynamic limit exists.
